beats.beat: The company sells four categories of specialty chemicals: Functional Additives (FA), Chemically Modified Minerals (CMM), Soft Minerals (SM), and Hard Minerals (HM). These are used across diverse industries such as paints, cosmetics, plastics, and construction.

The company has a long-term arrangement with its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited, to market and sell its products through the promoter's network. This dependence on a single channel is a key feature of its business model.

Revenue is concentrated: the top ten customers accounted for approximately 59% of revenue from operations in each of FY2015, FY2016, and FY2017. Exports to Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, and Sri Lanka contributed ₹1,068.18 lakh over the past five years.

Competitive strengths listed in the DRHP include a diversified product portfolio, diversified user industries, import substitution potential, support from the holding company, product innovation and R&D, and a strong management team.
The company does not have long-term or definitive agreements with customers or raw material suppliers, relying on purchase orders. This exposes it to volume and price volatility.

beats.beat: The DRHP includes restated financial statements for the six months ended September 30, 2017, and for each of the five fiscal years ended March 31, 2017, 2016, 2015, 2014, and 2013. All figures below are in ₹ lakh.

Profit after tax (PAT) turned positive from FY2015 onwards, after losses in the two preceding years: FY2013 (₹27.40 loss), FY2014 (₹12.17 loss), FY2015 (₹149.58 profit), FY2016 (₹90.18), FY2017 (₹174.82), and six months of FY2018 (₹132.75).
Basic earnings per share (EPS) followed the same pattern: ₹(0.45) in FY2013, ₹(0.20) in FY2014, ₹2.47 in FY2015, ₹1.46 in FY2016, ₹2.43 in FY2017, and ₹1.48 for the six months ended September 2017.

Total assets grew from ₹2,679.38 lakh in FY2014 to ₹3,424.96 lakh as of September 2017, after dipping to ₹2,592.53 lakh in FY2015. The latest assets include property, plant, and equipment as well as current assets.

Cash flow from operations has been volatile: positive in FY2016 (₹802.59 lakh) and FY2015 (₹422.36 lakh), but negative in FY2017 (₹349.75 outflow). For the six months ended September 2017, operating cash flow was positive ₹124.86 lakh.

Note: Revenue from operations is not explicitly extracted from the digest, so revenue trends and margins cannot be presented here. The DRHP may contain revenue numbers in the full restated financials.

beats.beat: The promoters are Mr. Chandresh S. Parikh, Mr. Atil C. Parikh, Mr. Rajesh C. Parikh, and corporate promoter 20 Microns Limited. Together they hold 89,48,270 equity shares, representing 99.76% of the pre-issue paid-up equity share capital.
Promoter group (excluding promoters) holds 21,510 equity shares, or 0.24% of pre-issue capital, meaning the public will hold a very small post-issue stake unless the offer is substantial.
The company has entered into related-party transactions in the past and may continue to do so. Details are provided in the financial statements on page 223 of the DRHP.

Compliance issues disclosed: past instances of non-filing or delayed filing of statutory forms with the ROC (subsequently filed with additional fees); certain licenses and registrations for the manufacturing facility at Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia have not been obtained; and the corporate logo is not registered.

beats.beat: The Indian specialty chemicals market (excluding agrochemicals and dyestuff) was estimated at about ₹1,000 billion in FY2017, according to CRISIL Research cited in the DRHP. The overall chemicals industry (excluding pharma and fertilisers) was ₹5,800–6,200 billion.

The specialty chemicals segment grew at a CAGR of 10–12% from FY2014 to FY2017, and CRISIL forecasts a 12–14% CAGR going forward. Sub-segments such as construction chemicals, water chemicals, and personal care ingredients are expected to grow at 15% CAGR.

The market is highly fragmented, with SMEs holding a 70–75% share, but global giants also compete. Only a few Indian players have the scale or capability to match global competitors on product development.

Key demand drivers include rising consumption, urbanisation (expected 36% urban population by 2020), and government initiatives such as the Draft National Chemical Policy, 100% FDI approval, and the implementation of GST from July 2017. Favourable global factors include China's stricter environmental norms pushing buyers to Indian sources.
The chemicals industry has been a net importer: imports grew at 6.4% CAGR while exports grew at 6% CAGR over FY2013–FY2017. Exports to Europe are subject to REACH regulations.

beats.beat: 20 Microns Nano Minerals Limited processes and sells specialty chemicals — primarily Functional Additives and Chemically Modified Minerals, along with Soft and Hard Minerals. It relies on a long-term arrangement with its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited, to market and sell its products through the promoter's network.

The company is raising funds via an initial public offer on the SME platform of NSE (NSE EMERGE) to finance capital expenditure for a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat, and for general corporate purposes.

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: who the company is, what it does, what it is raising and why it matters.

beats.beat: The IPO is a fresh issue of equity shares (the exact number and price band are not disclosed in the DRHP excerpts) to be listed on the SME platform of NSE (NSE EMERGE). The lead manager is Vivro Financial Services Private Limited and the registrar is Link Intime India Private Limited.

Proceeds will be used to fund capital expenditure for setting up a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat, and for general corporate purposes. Listing will also create a public market for the equity shares and enhance brand visibility.

offer.heading: The offer

beats.beat: No long-term customer or supplier agreements: The company relies on individual purchase orders, making revenue and supply vulnerable to sudden changes in demand or raw material availability.

Negative operating cash flow in FY2017: Despite turning profitable, the company recorded a net cash outflow of ₹349.75 lakh from operations in FY2017, indicating that profitability did not translate into cash generation that year.

Missing statutory licenses: The company has not obtained certain required registrations and approvals for its manufacturing facility at Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia, and may face penalties or operational disruptions.

Intense competition and pricing pressure: The fragmented specialty chemicals market includes both domestic SMEs and global players, and the company may need to cut prices to retain or attract customers.

Contingent liabilities and foreign exchange risk: As of September 30, 2017, contingent liabilities aggregated ₹29.11 lakh. Additionally, foreign currency exposure could harm cash flows and results if exchange rates move adversely.
